builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Controlled Knowledge Engineering for Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded LLM Agents and Runtime-Adaptive Policies
summary: TIGA replaces iterative free-form LLM prompting for taxonomy construction with an explicit-state, tool-grounded decision process using executable editing tools, interaction memory, and a runtime-adaptive policy. It costs substantially higher token consumption, API-call volume, and inference time relative to prompting baselines. It can fail to dominate on precision measures, and the benefit of the global reviewer component is dataset- and budget-dependent.
rationale: The method addresses a real production problem (structured taxonomy induction) but its benefits are inconsistent across metrics, its costs in tokens, API calls, and latency are substantial, and the reader's constrained budget and infrastructure make the trade-off unfavorable without further cost-reduction evidence.

claims.statement: TIGA replaces iterative free-form LLM prompting for taxonomy construction with an explicit-state, tool-grounded decision process using executable editing tools, interaction memory, and a runtime-adaptive policy. It costs substantially higher token consumption, API-call volume, and inference time relative to prompting baselines. It can fail to dominate on precision measures, and the benefit of the global reviewer component is dataset- and budget-dependent.

TIGA achieves the strongest structural-quality results in most evaluated configurations, but does not dominate on every precision measure; gains come with substantially higher token consumption, API-call volume, and inference time.
